items.title: Panama Francis interviewed by Michael Woods, Los Angeles, California, September 1, 1995
items.q: But I would meet him, like I meet you or somebody else and we’d talk and stuff, but not to play with him.

ctx.x: That’s great. Tell us what you know of Louis Armstrong.

I don’t know too much about Louis Armstrong. I knew him ‘cause see I was always in the position where I was always working, I didn’t have, I mean I didn’t have too much layoff time, and when Joe Glaser approached me about joining Louis, I asked him for a price. And he said “well no I don’t pay that kind of money.” So I said “well forget about it.” Because I was independent enough that I could say that. So that’s why I never worked with him. But I would meet him, like I meet you or somebody else and we’d talk and…
But you have played with some of the great Rhythm & Blues artists.

items.title: 61521_David Albert Francis oral history interview
items.q: Then I got the pleasure of being with him again in at Wildwood, New Jersey when he was with Louis Armstrong.

ctx.x: And, later on, when I came to New York, whenever he was in town, we used to hang out together every now and then, and I will never forget the time that I was out in California, and he had his own group at a club there, I think the club was called The Last Word, that was where I first saw Allen Eager -- Allen Eager was playing out there at the time.

And Sid and I used to hang out there, because at that time, he was doing very well for himself; I mean, as a leader. Then I got the pleasure of being with him again in at Wildwood, New Jersey when he was with Louis Armstrong. Louis Armstrong had Jack Teagarden T.
